title: Powerhouse targets high-level business intelligence in construction, not low-level industry data
content:
Positioning articulated by Wouter across both meetings:

Many industry tools already handle **low-level, specific data** well (3D geometry, quantities, schedules). What relies on manual, fragmented processes is **high-level business intelligence and document-heavy project management** — the layer of requirements documents, approvals, onboarding, risk registers, cost overviews (BAI weekly, 00:06:42).

The construction industry amplifies the opportunity: "nomad" teams that re-form per project, plus standardized requirements like BIM execution plans, mean **reusable document components** can standardize workflows across projects **without locking clients into a single proprietary platform** (00:09:54).

Supporting properties:
- **Local-first technology** emphasizes data protection — a direct fit for the sector's data-sovereignty constraints (EU-hosting requirements that prohibit some SaaS tools) and its rigid, heterogeneous stakeholder stacks (02:04:17)
- **Structured workflows, human-in-the-loop approvals, attributable history** address the siloed-data problem that limits AI effectiveness (00:01:06)
- Role: transform unstructured data into structured data to support business intelligence, reducing reliance on tools with excessive licensing costs (02:02:55)
description: Industry tools already handle low-level data. The gap is document-heavy, manual, fragmented PM — reusable document components standardize workflows without platform lock-in.
